conjunctionDays.title: Day 1 — Silence
conjunctionDays.summary: The Sun moves directly between Earth and Mars. Coronal plasma blinds high-gain signals. Radio static replaces Houston's voice.
conjunctionDays.event: Communication blackout initiated. Set initial habitat power profile.

choices.detail: Maintain normal internal lighting and background sensors.
Dim non-essential modules and throttle life-support buffer.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 2 — The Dust Front
conjunctionDays.summary: A massive regional dust storm envelops Jezero Crater. Atmospheric opacity tau rises to 3.8. Solar array output collapses by 65%.
conjunctionDays.event: Solar generation deficit. Power bus at negative net flow.

choices.detail: Suit up and deploy electrostatic brush to scrub photovoltaic panels. (High suit O2/battery cost + radiation exposure)
Fire up the Kilopower fission reserve. Conserves EVA suit life, but consumes reactor thermal isotopes.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 3 — Energy Crisis
conjunctionDays.summary: Primary storage battery bank cells experience thermal drop to -52°C. Power bus requires aggressive circuit shedding.
conjunctionDays.event: Sub-zero battery throttling. Select load shedding priority.

choices.detail: Preserves core life support and cryo-freezer. Food hydroponics take a hit.
Directs all heat to crew quarters. Jezero core samples warm slightly, endangering fragile organic chains.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 4 — Air Quality Warning
conjunctionDays.summary: CO2 amine scrubber bed differential pressure alarms. Cabin CO2 spikes to 2,800 ppm. Headache and cognitive slowing set in.

choices.detail: Guaranteed fix down to 500 ppm, but exhausts your only factory replacement.
Use thermal loop to regenerate fouled resin. Consumes 25 kWh power, partial recovery.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 5 — Water Shortage
conjunctionDays.summary: Graywater vacuum distillation centrifuge seals fail. Brackish brine leaks into filtration loop.
conjunctionDays.event: Water recycling stoppage. 60% daily loss rate without intervention.

choices.detail: Utilize synthesized perchlorate-resistant membranes from Act II research.
Halt hygiene loops and cut consumption to 1.2L per sol. Strains astronaut health.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 6 — Radiation Alert
conjunctionDays.summary: Satellite magnetometer detects Coronal Mass Ejection shockwave heading toward Mars. Surface radiation alert Level 3.
conjunctionDays.event: Solar Particle Event (SPE) incoming within 4 hours.

choices.text: Retreat into Storm Shelter Behind Water Bladders
choices.detail: Cram into central bunker shielded by habitat water tanks. Halts all activities for 24 hours.

choices.text: Reinforce Exterior Berm with Excavator EVA
choices.detail: Rush to heap fresh Martian regolith against hab hull. Absorbs more SPE energy but exposes explorer outside.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 7 — Halfway Point
conjunctionDays.summary: Seven days in the dark. Storm winds howl at 120 km/h against the habitat composite hull. Cabin systems groaning under fatigue.
conjunctionDays.event: Mid-point system audit and psychological stamina check.

choices.detail: Inspect every conduit, valve, and wiring harness. High calorie expenditure.
Rest for 14 hours to minimize metabolic O2 and food usage.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 8 — Mechanical Failure
conjunctionDays.summary: Exterior diagnostic camera confirms the stranded LREV chassis wheel hub has cracked from subzero thermal contraction.
conjunctionDays.event: Rover return to Gale is permanently impossible. Parts must be salvaged.

choices.text: Strip Rover Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Hab
choices.detail: Braving the exterior cold to haul rover cells inside. Adds +35% permanent battery capacity to the shelter.

choices.text: Preserve Rover Chassis as Pressurized Refuge
choices.detail: Leave LREV intact as secondary emergency airlock backup in case hab ruptures.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 9 — Emergency Supply Cache
conjunctionDays.summary: Automated orbital tracking detects the pre-positioned autonomous cargo pod parachute signature 400m east of the habitat.
conjunctionDays.event: Cargo drop confirmed in boulder field.

choices.detail: Navigate zero-visibility dust storm to retrieve emergency O2 cylinders and filtration seals.
Do not risk EVA in near-zero visibility. Cargo remains untouched.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 10 — The Last Battery
conjunctionDays.summary: Habitat primary capacitor bank shorts due to fine electrostatic dust infiltration. Power drops to emergency baseline.
conjunctionDays.event: Severe power deficit. Direct fission link required.

choices.text: Re-route Kilopower Fission Directly to ECLSS
choices.detail: Focuses all power strictly into Life Support and Heating. Cryo-freezer must run at bare minimum.
Sacrifices cabin heat (drops to 4°C) to keep sample temperatures at -70°C.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 11 — The Autonomous Supply Rover
conjunctionDays.summary: An unmanned NASA exploration crawler programmed prior to conjunction arrives at the habitat airlock bearing heavy spares.
conjunctionDays.event: Spare parts delivered to airlock vestibule.

choices.detail: Use new seals to re-pressurize the science lab and airlocks.

choices.text: Consolidate into Compact Emergency Living Module
choices.detail: Keep outer bulkheads sealed off. Low power and heating footprint for the remainder of the mission.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 12 — The Final Check
conjunctionDays.summary: Atmospheric pressure begins gradual recovery. Dust opacity falls from 3.8 to 1.9. Solar panels start generating weak morning current.
conjunctionDays.event: Prepare scientific data package for upcoming burst transmission.

choices.detail: Encodes all Arcadia polygonal scans, isotope profiles, and Jezero astrobiology mass-spec spectra.
Focuses solely on habitat survival telemetry and crew medical logs.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 13 — Waiting
conjunctionDays.summary: The Martian sky clears from blood orange to dusty amber. The roar of the wind drops to a faint whistle against the airlock.
conjunctionDays.event: Last sol of full silence. Mental discipline and system check.

choices.detail: Verify alignment coords for Deep Space Network (DSN) Madrid, Goldstone, and Canberra stations.
Walk the perimeter to inspect foundation pilings and antenna array.

conjunctionDays.title: Day 14 — The Signal
conjunctionDays.summary: Mars emerges from behind the solar disk. Plasma diffraction falls below carrier threshold. The high-gain antenna light flickers from amber to solid green.
conjunctionDays.event: CARRIER LOCK ACQUIRED. Deep Space Network incoming signal.

choices.text: Transmit Full Mission & Survival Archive to Earth
choices.detail: Stream all telemetry, survival records, and astrobiology sample telemetry to Houston.
